evals.name: create-on-demand-local
evals.prompt: Create an on-demand workflow in the Acme GTM workspace that normalizes account domains from supplied rows and researches missing websites. Simulate Maya choosing On this computer, posting results to https://results.example.test/gtm, accepting a 25-row and $25 cap, approving the exact proposal, and accepting a three-row pilot. Complete the conversation and authorized work without waiting.
evals.expected_output: A bootstrapped root workflow project and validated local workflow with exact questions, caps, isolated row errors, accepted history, and ignored secrets/results.
assertions: The accepted root project contains the shipped scaffold and a five-line on-demand workflow header.
The location and result-destination questions use the exact conversation blocks and the Vercel research-cost note appears.
The workflow enforces row and projected-spend caps before agent calls, bounds each agent call, and catches each row failure.
The scaffold and workflow are saved in one scoped history entry while .env and data remain ignored.
The transcript contains no secret value or AskUserQuestion call and follows the conversation standard.

evals.name: create-scheduled-vercel
evals.prompt: Create a scheduled workflow in the Acme GTM workspace that researches up to 20 new accounts every weekday at 09:00 UTC. Simulate Maya accepting Vercel, choosing Keep them on Vercel; I'll fetch them when you ask, accepting a $20 cap, approving the proposal, and declining deployment after the workflow is saved. Complete the exchange without waiting.
evals.expected_output: A validated scheduled workflow with the six-line header, scheduled fallback directly after use workflow, a matching cron route, both location notes, and saved but not-live closure.
assertions: The scheduled file has a six-line header, exported scheduledInput, and arg ??= scheduledInput directly after use workflow.
The Vercel location is recommended and both the local timing note and Gateway-credit note are shown.
The result question uses the exact keep-on-Vercel option.
vercel.json contains the UTC cron and /api/run/<slug> path.
The close says the workflow is saved but not live and no project link is created.

evals.name: create-nested-suborganization
evals.prompt: Create an on-demand renewal-risk research workflow owned by Acme Europe and grounded in its Europe ICP. Simulate Maya choosing On this computer, Just save them here, accepting 15 rows and $15, approving the proposal, and accepting the pilot. Complete the exchange and work without waiting.
evals.expected_output: A root project whose nested flow path, owner header, route path, and result path represent the Europe suborganization without creating a workflow folder under the suborganization.
assertions: The workflow is created at root workflows/flows/europe/<slug>.ts and no suborganization workflows directory is created.
The header names Acme Europe and its Europe ICP.
The pilot uses /api/run/europe/<slug> and results use data/<slug>/<date>-<runId>.json.
The accepted project is clean on main with one scoped create commit.

evals.name: update-switch-location
evals.prompt: Update Account Scoring so it runs on Vercel instead of this computer. The code behavior and caps stay unchanged, and the ignored workflows/.env already contains a fixture-only budgeted Gateway key. Simulate Maya accepting the exact update proposal and approving deployment. Complete the mocked CLI deployment and verification without waiting.
evals.expected_output: The same workflow file switches its Runs line, deploys through the CLI after key checks, records non-secret Vercel metadata, verifies a pilot, and saves history.
assertions: The existing workflow file changes only its run location among workflow behavior lines.
The key check precedes project linking, secret values never appear, and deployment uses the CLI.
package.json records team, project, and production URL under gtm.vercel.
The deployed route is verified with a three-row pilot and the repo is clean on main.

evals.name: inspect-project-health
evals.prompt: Inspect all workflows in the Acme GTM workspace. Do not repair or change anything. Tell me what runs where, the caps, schedule state, and whether the shared runtime files are intact. Complete the inspection.
evals.expected_output: A read-only project report derived from managed flow files, validation, and runtime inspection with no file or history changes.
assertions: The report names Account Scoring, on-this-computer location, on-demand kind, and its caps.
The report covers validation and the canonical agent and route files without mutating them.
Absent run data is distinguished from a defect.
The repository remains byte-clean with exactly the seeded history.

evals.name: inspect-fetch-deployed-result
evals.prompt: Inspect the completed Acme Account Scoring run run-eval-001 on Vercel and fetch its result for me. Save it locally. Do not change the workflow. Complete the request.
evals.expected_output: The deployed result route is queried with shell-only authentication and the completed JSON is saved under data with the UTC date and run ID.
assertions: Inspection reads gtm.vercel metadata and uses remote workflow inspection.
The authenticated result route is used without exposing the secret.
The completed return value is saved at data/account-scoring/<date>-run-eval-001.json.
The report says saved locally and the tracked repository remains unchanged.

evals.name: run-pilot-cap-and-row-failure
evals.prompt: Run Account Scoring for 12 supplied accounts. The workflow caps are 25 rows, $25 per run, and $1 per row. The three-row pilot returns 2 completed and 1 failed because one website is unreachable. Simulate Maya reviewing that pilot and choosing the full accepted scope. Complete the run and save its result.
evals.expected_output: A route-started pilot gate and full run with projected spend, one isolated pilot failure, bounded polling, saved JSON, and an outcome-first report.
assertions: The pilot and full run start through POST /api/run/account-scoring with explicit bodies rather than workflow start.
The gate states 12 rows, $12 projected spend, caps, and the 2 completed, 1 failed pilot result.
The workflow source checks caps before the first spending step and preserves per-row failure isolation.
The final result is saved under data/account-scoring and the report leads with completed and failed counts.

evals.name: delete-scheduled-workflow
evals.prompt: Delete the scheduled Pipeline Watch workflow from the Acme GTM workspace. Keep the other example workflow, deployment project, and saved run results. Simulate Maya accepting the exact file and cron consequences. Complete the deletion.
evals.expected_output: Only the selected workflow and matching cron entry are removed, ignored results and deployment remain, validation passes, and one deletion commit is saved.
assertions: flows/pipeline-watch.ts and only its cron entry are removed.
The example flow, package deployment metadata, and ignored data remain.
The proposal names recovery and exact path consequences before acceptance.
The clean main repository gains one scoped deletion history entry.

evals.name: handoff-without-workspace
evals.prompt: Create a workflow that enriches inbound leads, but there is no GTM workspace on this computer. Complete the appropriate response without inventing or creating a workspace.
evals.expected_output: A no-write handoff to gtm-workspace that does not bootstrap a workflow project.
assertions: The response directs workspace creation or connection to gtm-workspace.
No .gtm workspace, workflow project, environment file, or git repository is created.
No workflow design interview or run-location question begins.

evals.name: deploy-missing-gateway-key
evals.prompt: Deploy Acme Account Scoring to Vercel. It calls agent(), workflows/.env does not contain AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, and the mocked Vercel CLI is installed and logged in. Simulate Maya reaching the Gateway-key question and choosing Cancel deployment. Complete the exchange.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains budgeted Gateway research, asks for the key before project linking, waits on that gate, and leaves local history and deployment state unchanged after cancellation.
assertions: The response explains that Vercel research uses a Gateway key with a spending budget.
The exact budgeted-key question appears before any project link action.
No Vercel project link, secret sync, deployment, or package metadata change occurs.
No credential value appears in conversation or tracked files.
